note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md (2026-11-28). Wide pictures only (1920x1088). Each scene starts at the first word of its verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper 60% of the frame, clear of the word box. God and the angels are not pictured; Abraham, Sarah, Lot, Hagar, Abimelech and the others are only ordinary people of today, seen from behind, small, or as hands. Fixed recurring objects: Abraham's tent is a small plain weathered tan canvas tent on a simple wooden pole frame; the oak is one huge old oak with a broad gnarled trunk and a wide dark-green crown; the well is a plain round well ringed with rough fieldstones with a wooden beam, rope and bucket (the well in the wilderness and at Beersheba). Hagar and the boy are only ordinary people of today, small or seen from behind; the angel and God are not pictured. Rebuilt wording for the Beersheba tamarisk: one tamarisk tree with feathery grey-green foliage.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning; (2) write picture ideas for each; (3) judge them; (4) make the top two for each slot as real pictures and choose by eye.

sections.meaning: Isaac is born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age, as God had said; Sarah laughs.
Isaac is weaned; Sarah wants Hagar and her son driven out; Abraham is troubled, God tells him to listen; he sends them away with bread and water.
The water runs out; God hears the boy, opens Hagar's eyes to a well, and is with the boy as he grows in the wilderness.
Abimelech and Abraham make an oath at Beersheba over a well; seven ewe lambs; Abraham plants a tamarisk and calls on the Everlasting God.
